guidance: plane_repair.py detects and repairs split planes itself; run it before hand-crafting jumpers.
Always refill zones after copper edits on plane layers (kicad-cli pcb drc --refill-zones --save-board).
plane_repair/route_cleanup mutate the board in place and self-detect regressions (exit 1): on exit 1 restore the pre-fix snapshot (state.py restore) and report.

violations.msg: J2 pin 1 (+3V3) is SOLID-connected to 1199.221 mm2 of 1 oz pour and is then hand-soldered: measured, its full 3.142 mm2 is merged into the zone with copper on 72/72 of a ring at r=1.6 mm. constraints.json planes sets connect 'solid' for the F.Cu +3V3 zone, which is correct and load-bearing for U1's tab, but it applies zone-wide and J2 is a through-hole screw terminal that requirements.md s.7 says is hand soldered after PCBA. The iron cannot raise the pad against that plane: the outcome is a cold joint on the 3.3 V output pin or an overheated board. Every other hand-soldered pin is fine (J1.2 and J2.2 already get 4-spoke relief from the B.Cu zone, J1.1 is isolated on both layers) - J2.1 is the single exception. Fix: per-pad (zone_connect 1) on J2.1 only; it sits 17.49 mm from the tab, outside check_thermal's 14.33 mm reach entirely, and the relief costs ~2.93 mm2 of pour in the partial-effectiveness band - thermally free. If left as-is, put a preheat note in the assembly instructions.

scope: fix ONLY these violations; do not touch unrelated nets/regions; re-run the failed gate when done
